annotation_description: On turn 3 with 3 lands available (Spirebluff Canal, Riverpyre Verge, and the Verge can tap for U if controlling an Island or Mountain - Spirebluff Canal counts as neither type, so Riverpyre Verge only taps for R), the player has Duelist of the Mind (1U) which is a key tempo creature in this deck. With Spirebluff Canal providing U and Riverpyre Verge providing R, the player actually has 1R+1U available, which is enough to cast Duelist of the Mind (1U, paying 1 generic with R). Deploying Duelist on turn 3 adds a flying vigilance threat that synergizes with the draw-heavy gameplan and Stormchaser's Talent. Passing without casting anything wastes mana and tempo.

The opponent has no creatures on the battlefield (their graveyard contains lands and a sorcery, and no battlefield creatures are listed). The Otter Token is a 1/1 with prowess that could attack freely for 1 damage with zero risk. There's no reason to hold back a free attack into an empty board.

Casting Duelist of the Mind in the precombat main phase is suboptimal. Duelist's power equals the number of cards drawn this turn, which is currently 0 (assuming the draw for turn already happened, it would be 1). Playing it pre-combat means it will likely attack as a 1/3 or 0/3. More importantly, casting a creature before combat when holding tricks like Into the Flood Maw and Torch the Tower is generally worse than attacking first with the Otter token (which has prowess and could benefit from post-combat spells). Additionally, Fear of Missing Out could have been a stronger play here — it provides a 2/3 body, triggers a loot on ETB which could help fuel delirium, and with delirium active it grants extra combat phases. Frostcliff Siege (choosing Jeskai) would also have been worth considering as it draws cards on combat damage, synergizing with the Otter already on board.

The opponent has no creatures on the battlefield and no untapped lands visible to threaten interaction. Attacking with the 1/1 Otter Token is free damage with zero risk — there's nothing to block it. The Otter is a 1/1 prowess token that could also benefit from spells cast in second main. Additionally, with Frostcliff Siege (Jeskai mode) potentially coming down later, establishing a pattern of connecting with combat damage matters. Missing 1 damage repeatedly adds up, and there's no downside to attacking here against an empty board.

Playing Tiger-Seal in the precombat main phase is debatable. Tiger-Seal taps itself at the beginning of your upkeep and only untaps when you draw your second card each turn. With Frostcliff Siege (Jeskai mode) on the battlefield, combat damage draws a card, but Tiger-Seal won't be able to attack this turn anyway since it's a new creature without haste. More importantly, casting Tiger-Seal before combat means the Otter Token and Duelist of the Mind won't benefit from prowess triggers during combat this turn. If instead the player attacked first with the Otter and Duelist (Duelist has 0 power since no cards drawn yet this turn, but Otter could attack), then cast Tiger-Seal post-combat, the sequencing would be slightly better. Additionally, casting Duelist of the Mind #2 might have been considered as an alternative play, though Tiger-Seal is a reasonable card to deploy. The main issue is casting a creature before combat when there's no urgency, potentially missing prowess value from combat tricks.

Cast Duelist of the Mind with only 2 untapped lands, leaving 0 mana open, when they had Multiversal Passage in hand to play first. Playing the land first would leave 1 mana open to hold up Into the Flood Maw or Torch the Tower as interaction.

Declined to attack into a completely empty board. The opponent has no creatures to block. Even without pre-combat spell casting, attacking with Fear of Missing Out (2/3), Otter Token (1/1), and any Duelists with non-zero power deals free damage and triggers Frostcliff Siege (Jeskai) to draw a card on combat damage. Skipping combat entirely wastes significant damage and card advantage.

Cast Boomerang Basics in postcombat main phase before playing Riverpyre Verge from hand. The reasoning about lethal is completely wrong since combat already happened - no prowess triggers or power boosts matter this turn. Should have played land first to maximize available mana for additional spells this turn.

annotation_description: Discarding Into the Flood Maw (a 1-mana interactive spell that triggers prowess and can bounce future threats) when holding two redundant lands (Riverpyre Verge and Spirebluff Canal) with already 5+ lands on board. The cheap spell has more utility than extra land drops at this stage of the game.

Opponent is at 6 life with no board. Casting Stormchaser's Talent (U) creates a new untapped Otter token with prowess and pumps Duelist (via drawing with Frostcliff Siege Jeskai on combat damage). Casting Boomerang Basics on own permanent draws a card (increasing Duelist's power) and triggers prowess on Otters. By chaining spells pre-combat, Duelist of the Mind's power could reach 2-3+ with flying/vigilance, plus fresh Otter tokens attacking, potentially threatening lethal or near-lethal against an empty board at 6 life.
